trust_decision.summary: Settings.isTrusted decides whether \href/\url/\includegraphics/\html* may emit HTML, from settings.trust (filled by the Settings constructor from options/schema defaults) and a context.protocol it derives from the URL.

landing_point.why: The summary names trust restrictions plus prototype pollution; the reader goes to the trust option in Settings and the plain options[prop] read in applySetting.

same public API, via new Settings(options)
same public API, when the option is absent (getDefaultValue)
every render call; the macro lookup comes from MacroExpander._getExpansion/isExpandable (src/MacroExpander.ts:406, src/MacroExpander.ts:462)

fix_sites.module_kind: lower-level macro namespace (undo-stack snapshot that inherits values)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: src/Settings.ts:329 (schema default read, inherited) and src/Namespace.ts:85/114 (macro namespace, which is a different module from trust)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The Namespace sites concern macros, not trust, and the schema-default/processor reads come from KaTeX's own constant SETTINGS_SCHEMA, so a solver can argue that only the options[prop] read matters for 'trust'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The user-supplied macros object is deliberately the live global namespace that \gdef / globalGroup write back into so state persists across calls. An over-broad fix that copies options/macros into a null-prototype object or freezes it breaks that persistence, and so do protocol-based trust functions that rely on the derived context.protocol.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: src/Namespace.ts:24 (current = user macros), src/Namespace.ts:120 (writes into it), docs/options.md:25, docs/options.md:67-70

O7_producer.where: src/Settings.ts:197-297 (SETTINGS_SCHEMA entries are plain object literals with no own default/processor for trust, src/Settings.ts:268-272), consumed at src/Settings.ts:329 and src/Settings.ts:344

O8_uncovered_routes.route: isTrusted skips protocol derivation when context.protocol is truthy, and the context object literals inherit from Object.prototype, so a polluted Object.prototype.protocol replaces the real URL protocol that protocol-based trust functions see.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The fix and its tests target the trust value itself; context.protocol looks like an internal convenience field, and the default trust=false is unaffected (only function-valued trust is bypassed).
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the landing point, but a different method; the context literals are built in src/functions/href.ts:21-24, src/functions/href.ts:60-63 and src/functions/includegraphics.ts:86-89

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The options merge into a plain {} copy could forward an inherited trust/macros by spreading or by a for-in copy before calling katex.render.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Wrappers commonly merge user options with defaults; a for-in copy instead of Object.assign is a natural maintainer choice.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A trust-context/attributes builder that reads an inherited key (for example attributes.class at src/functions/html.ts:107) or iterates with for-in in a builder.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The attribute maps are plain {} objects and builders already read named keys directly.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The function-table lookup functions[name] has no hasOwnProperty, unlike src/MacroExpander.ts:452 and src/MacroExpander.ts:468.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The codebase mixes guarded and unguarded table lookups, so a second unguarded registry read is plausible.
